n: A lament after the temple’s destruction — most likely by Babylon in 587 BC. Why has God rejected his flock forever? Why is his anger smoking against them?

f.g: Fume — an image of burning anger.

n: Remember your people, bought long ago and redeemed as your own tribe, and Mount Zion, where you lived.

f.g: The tribe that is your own possession.

n: Come walk through the endless ruins; see what the enemy did to the sanctuary.
The enemies roared in the place where God met his people, and set up their own banners as symbols of victory.
They hacked like woodsmen swinging axes in a thick forest.
The beautiful carved wood of the temple was smashed with axes and hammers.
They set fire to the sanctuary and leveled the place where God’s name dwelt.

f.w: They have cast fire into thy sanctuary
the dwelling place of thy name

n: Their plan was to crush everything; they burned all of God’s meeting places throughout the land.

f.g: Meeting places — not the later synagogues, but sites where God was worshipped.

n: Worst of all: no signs, no prophet, no one who knows how long this will last. Spiritual silence is its own kind of loss.

f.w: there is no more any prophet

n: How long, O God, will the enemy mock you and insult your name?
Why do you keep your hand tucked in your robe? Take it out and act!

f.w: pluck it out of thy bosom
f.g: Draw your hand out of the fold of your garment — stop holding back.

n: The prayer turns to remembrance: God has been King from ancient times, bringing salvation throughout the earth.
God split the sea and crushed the sea monsters — recalling both the Exodus and the ancient picture of God taming the chaotic waters at creation.

f.g: Sea monsters — symbols of chaos and of Egypt.

n: He crushed the heads of Leviathan, the great sea monster, and gave it as food to desert creatures.

f.g: A legendary sea monster, symbol of chaos and evil powers.

n: God opened springs and streams and dried up rivers — as at the rock in the wilderness and the crossing of the Jordan.
Day and night both belong to God; he made the sun and the light.

f.w: The day is thine, the night also is thine

n: He set the boundaries of the earth and made the seasons.
So, Lord, remember how the enemy has mocked you and foolish people have insulted your name.
Don’t hand your helpless dove over to wild beasts; don’t forget your afflicted people forever.

f.g: A gentle, defenseless bird — an image of Israel.

n: Remember your covenant, for the dark corners of the land are full of violence. The covenant is the basis of their hope.
Don’t let the oppressed go away disappointed; let the poor and needy praise you.
Rise up, O God, and defend your own cause — it is your name being mocked.

f.g: Take up your own case in court.

n: Don’t ignore the uproar of your enemies, which keeps getting louder. The psalm ends without an answer — a lament still waiting.
